name: Keystatic
title: Mica vs. Keystatic
summary: Both are Git-backed, database-free editors with a TypeScript model and an Astro integration. Keystatic saves each edit as a commit on GitHub and offers an optional cloud. Mica uses plain Git with no host API, saves drafts and publishes them as one commit. Keystatic suits teams that live on GitHub.

chooseMica.text: Your content is on a Git host other than GitHub.
Editors should save drafts, then publish several changes as one commit with a summary.
Editors should see the real Astro page beside the form, with a click on the page that moves the cursor to the field.
You want to run the editor on your own machine or in a container that you run, with no GitHub App.
You want AI agents to save drafts through a built-in MCP server.

chooseOther.text: Your team already works on GitHub, and you want editors to save on branches.
Editors should review changes in GitHub pull requests.
You want Keystatic Cloud, so that editors need no server that you run.
Editors should work together in real time: Keystatic Cloud Pro has an experimental multiplayer mode.

facts.value: Yes. GitHub only; GitLab support is an open request. Local mode edits files on disk.
Hosted service available: Keystatic Cloud, optional. Self-hosting possible: local mode, or GitHub mode with your own GitHub App and API routes on a Node or SSR host.
MIT. Keystatic Cloud is free up to 3 users; Pro costs from $10 a month plus $5 for each extra user.
Yes. Official @keystatic/astro. It needs React, Markdoc and an SSR adapter. Content comes through Content Collections or the Reader API.
GitHub App OAuth. Editors need write access on GitHub, or a fork path.
Each save is one commit to the current branch. Editors can create branches. A protected branch leads to a new branch. No batch publish is documented.
No preview pane. A previewUrl link opens a Next.js draft-mode page after a save to a branch; the documented recipe is for the Next.js App Router. Issues #1071 and #1447 are open.
Not supported. Pull request #1514 is open.
Not documented. The relationship field links to entries by slug.
Not documented as a feature. Issues #1553 and #1080 are open.
No roles of its own. GitHub permissions apply. Review goes through GitHub pull requests.
Not documented. The documentation mentions no MCP server and no agent support.
